title: Potato, baked, peel eaten, with cheese

content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato with the peel left on and cheese is a popular dish that combines the tender interior of a baked tuber, the flavorful crisp of the skin, and melted cheese. The peel retains most of the nutrients, while the cheese adds protein and a rich taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potato skin contains more fiber, vitamin C, and potassium than the flesh alone.
Baking preserves more antioxidants than boiling.
Cheeses commonly used are high‑calcium varieties such as cheddar or parmesan.
In many cuisines the baked potato is seasoned with herbs like rosemary or thyme for extra aroma.
Potatoes are one of the world’s most consumed root vegetables, with over 350 million tonnes produced annually.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: The skin provides a substantial amount of dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C in the skin helps boost immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Baked potatoes release glucose slowly, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Potatoes contain carotenoids and phenolic compounds that combat free radicals.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to cheese, especially if it contains lactose.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Cheese adds calories and saturated fat; portion size should be monitored.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheese is often salty; people with hypertension should choose low‑salt options.

items.title: Salt on the skin
items.content: The peel is frequently seasoned with salt before baking; excess sodium may be undesirable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wash the potatoes, leave the skin on, cut them in half, brush with olive oil, sprinkle grated cheese, and bake until the cheese is golden and the skin is crisp. Serve hot, optionally topped with herbs or a dollop of sour cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw potatoes in a cool, dark place. Keep the cooked baked potatoes in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. When reheating, add a little oil to restore the crispness of the skin.
